Title: API
QuestionDetail: What does API stand for?
AnswerDetails: Application Programming Interface. The contract one piece of software offers another: what you can ask for, and what you get back.

Title: Who Made Python
QuestionDetail: Which language did Guido van Rossum create?
AnswerDetails: Python, released in 1991. He named it after Monty Python's Flying Circus, not the snake.

Title: The First iPhone
QuestionDetail: In which year did the first iPhone go on sale?
AnswerDetails: 2007. Announced in January, on sale in June, and it reset what a phone was expected to be.

Title: HTTP
QuestionDetail: What does HTTP stand for?
AnswerDetails: HyperText Transfer Protocol — the request-and-response convention every web page still travels on.

Title: Who Wrote Git
QuestionDetail: Who created the Git version control system?
AnswerDetails: Linus Torvalds, in 2005, after the Linux kernel project lost access to the proprietary tool it had been using. He wrote the first working version in about ten days.

Title: One Byte
QuestionDetail: What is the largest value a single unsigned byte can hold?
AnswerDetails: 255. Eight bits gives 256 distinct values, and counting starts at zero.

Title: EC2
QuestionDetail: Which cloud provider's compute service is called EC2?
AnswerDetails: Amazon Web Services. EC2 stands for Elastic Compute Cloud and launched in 2006.

Title: SQL
QuestionDetail: What does SQL stand for?
AnswerDetails: Structured Query Language, the standard way to ask a relational database for data.

Title: Twenty Percent Time
QuestionDetail: Which company became famous for letting engineers spend a fifth of their time on projects of their own choosing?
AnswerDetails: Google. Gmail and AdSense are the examples usually cited, though the policy has been much reduced since.

Title: Amazon's Rules
QuestionDetail: What does Amazon call the set of principles it hires and promotes against?
AnswerDetails: Leadership Principles. There are sixteen, and Amazon interviews explicitly against them.

Title: Move Fast
QuestionDetail: Which company's early internal motto was 'Move fast and break things'?
AnswerDetails: Facebook, now Meta. It was retired in 2014 in favour of 'Move fast with stable infrastructure'.

Title: The Netflix Deck
QuestionDetail: What phrase titles Netflix's famous culture document?
AnswerDetails: Freedom and Responsibility. The 2009 slide deck was downloaded millions of times and shaped a generation of startup HR policy.

Title: No Managers
QuestionDetail: Which retailer famously adopted holacracy, removing traditional managers company-wide?
AnswerDetails: Zappos, from 2013. Holacracy itself was developed by Brian Robertson; Zappos was its most prominent large-scale adopter, and around 18% of staff took a buyout rather than continue.

Title: OKR
QuestionDetail: What does OKR stand for?
AnswerDetails: Objectives and Key Results. The method came out of Intel under Andy Grove and spread through Google.

Title: Day 1
QuestionDetail: Which company's founder insisted it always be 'Day 1'?
AnswerDetails: Amazon. Jeff Bezos used the phrase from the first shareholder letter onward; Day 2, in his telling, is stasis followed by decline.

Title: The Web Proposal
QuestionDetail: In which year did Tim Berners-Lee write the proposal that became the World Wide Web?
AnswerDetails: 1989. The first website went live in 1991.

Title: The Analytical Engine
QuestionDetail: Who designed the Analytical Engine, the first design for a general-purpose programmable computer?
AnswerDetails: Charles Babbage, in the 1830s. It was never built in his lifetime; Ada Lovelace wrote the notes describing how it could be programmed.

Title: Images in the Browser
QuestionDetail: Which 1993 browser popularised inline images and kicked off the web's first growth surge?
AnswerDetails: Mosaic, from NCSA. Its team went on to build Netscape Navigator.

Title: The First Microprocessor
QuestionDetail: Which company shipped the first commercial microprocessor, the 4004?
AnswerDetails: Intel, in 1971.

Title: The Bitcoin Paper
QuestionDetail: In which year was the Bitcoin whitepaper published?
AnswerDetails: 2008. The first block was mined in January 2009.

Title: SpaceX
QuestionDetail: Who founded SpaceX?
AnswerDetails: Elon Musk, in 2002.

Title: A Billion Users
QuestionDetail: Which platform was the first to reach one billion monthly users?
AnswerDetails: Facebook, in October 2012.

Title: The First Email
QuestionDetail: In which year did Ray Tomlinson send the first networked email, choosing @ to separate user from machine?
AnswerDetails: 1971, on ARPANET.

Title: IoT
QuestionDetail: What does IoT stand for?
AnswerDetails: Internet of Things — everyday devices with network connections and, usually, an update problem.

Title: Under Bitcoin
QuestionDetail: Which underlying technology do Bitcoin and similar currencies rely on?
AnswerDetails: A blockchain: an append-only ledger replicated across many machines.

Title: GPT
QuestionDetail: What does the GPT in ChatGPT stand for?
AnswerDetails: Generative Pre-trained Transformer. The transformer architecture was published by Google researchers in 2017.

Title: CI/CD
QuestionDetail: What does CI/CD stand for?
AnswerDetails: Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery, or Deployment. Integrate small changes often; ship them automatically.

Title: Closer to the Source
QuestionDetail: What is the term for processing data near where it is generated rather than in a central region?
AnswerDetails: Edge computing. It trades centralised control for lower latency and less data in flight.

Title: SaaS
QuestionDetail: What does SaaS stand for?
AnswerDetails: Software as a Service — software you rent and access over the network rather than install and own.
